items.title: 66086_Zilner T. Randolph oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions 'Big Chief' only as part of a joke/story told by the interviewer about a musician changing songs. The interviewee does not mention Big Chief, nor does the interviewee describe any personal interaction or relationship with Big Chief.

ctx.x: Yeah, he did, he cried, because it was his mother's favorite hymn, but he was going to get back at me and play his mother's favorite hymn, but in playing it, he began to -- I guess, think about his mother while he was playing it, and then he cries, because I think his mother had passed or something at the time. So the boys really kidded him about that. That was a funny thing. But he would always do that. And if I would say -- if I'd ask him to play any sweet number, he'd change it.

One time, I called a number that I wanted him to play and he changed it to a Indian Love Call. And he forgot the Indian Love Call, so the boys said he had all the little braves coming out, Big Chief, Sitting Bull and all of them. They really kidded him, so -- but he never did stop changing those numbers.
Well, how often did you work? Did you work every day?
